newsitem.title: GERMANY: German share traders fear recovery may be hollow.
newsitem.headline: German share traders fear recovery may be hollow.

text.p: German shares traded in or around intraday highs on Wednesday, bouyed by the strength of the dollar at 1.71 marks and a strong overnight close on Wall Street, but dealers feared that the gains lacked substance.
At 1303 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 44.45 points, 1.34 percent, at 3,372.58 points, not far off an intraday high of 3,376.90 points.

"This is reverse engines on last week and seems to be much more-futures driven than retail-driven as far as I can see. There isn't that much buying interest around full-stop," said a London-based trader.

"It could be a bit of a dead-cat bounce -- no-one trusts the market but no-one can afford not be part of the rise," the trader said. A "dead cat bounce" is slang for market rebound lacking in substance and is generally viewed with suspicion.
A Frankfurt dealer said: "The market is very selective today. Wall Street, the debt market and the dollar are being supportive, but volumes are very thin."

Much in the limelight over the course of the day were Bavarian banks Bayerische Hypo-Bank and Bayerische Vereinsbank, as the long-running theme of takeovers or mergers in the German banking sector reappeared on the scene.

"Hypo-Bank denied during the session that there were signs of a single investor amassing a stake in it, but everyone still thinks it is in the firing line -- if not today, then soon, so the takeover speculation continues," the London trader said.
Another sector in the limelight was the car industry. BMW AG was up 63.40 marks, 4.71 percent, at 1,410 marks, jsut shy of an all-time high of 1,415 marks.

The share was said to be still enjoying positive sentiment after analysts revised their earnings outlook for BMW upwards last month. The dollar strength also helped boost the car sector, traditionally strong exporters.
Volkswagen AG was up 26.10 marks, 2.83 percent, at 946.10 marks in afternoon trade.
Shares in FMC, the dialysis subsidiary of German medical Tuesday's analysts' meeting.

FMC shares were up 7.70 marks, 5.2 percent, at 155.80 marks. Neither FMC nor its parent Fresenius AG profited much from positive figures on Tuesday, and dealers said there was an element of catch-up in the share's positive performance.
Fresenius preference shares also outperformed the market, up 17.50 marks, or 4.86 percent at 377.50 marks.
"Long-term the outlook for this market is positive because of the levels of liquidity in the market, but domestic investors are still holding off at these levels," the Frankfurt dealer said.
He anticipated a range in the mid-term of 3,150 and 3,450 points for the DAX.
